# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** About thirty or thirty-five years old  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Origin:** Ontario (Toronto)  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Role:** Newspaper man and novelist  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v5 c2 P67](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0067)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen is tall and broad-shouldered with thick brown hair, a finely-cut nose and chin, and large, brilliant dark-gray eyes. He knows how to dress well, though he looks as if life has not been completely easy for him.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)_

## Personality

Owen possesses a pleasant voice and a delightful smile. He is passionate and dedicated regarding his literary work, eagerly collaborating with others when inspired. He is emotionally open with trusted confidantes.

_Sources: [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)_

## Traits

- Pleasant voice  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- Delightful smile  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- Passionate about writing  <sub>[v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

## Abilities

- Short story and book writing  <sub>[v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)</sub>
- Photography  <sub>[v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)</sub>

## Goals

- Finding the essential central idea and soul to write a novel  <sub>[v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

## History

After recovering from typhoid in the spring, Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds upon his doctor's advice to visit his grandparents' old home and seek inspiration for a novel. During his stay, he met Captain Jim Boyd and collaborated with him to write a book titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim, gathering its central material in Four Winds. While in the area, he fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore and confessed his feelings to Anne Blythe. Although he had to return to his work in Vancouver, he later returned to Four Winds to court Leslie. After their courtship, Owen and Leslie married and had children. They subsequently arranged a year-long trip to Japan so Owen could gather material for a new novel with a Japanese setting.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c34 P30](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0030), [v4 c36 P27](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0027), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v5 c2 P67](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0067), [v5 c2 P68](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0068)_

## Background by volume

- Grandson of John Selwyn, the schoolmaster who built the house in Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Suffered a bad spell of typhoid fever in the spring and was ordered to the sea by his doctor  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Wrote short stories for magazines alongside newspaper work  <sub>[v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

## Quotes

> Alack-a-day, no. I’ve never been able to get the right central idea for it. It lurks beyond me—it allures—and beckons—and recedes—I almost grasp it and it is gone. Perhaps amid this peace and loveliness, I shall be able to capture it. Miss Bryant tells me that you write.  <sub>[v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020)</sub>

> I dare say it is beyond me as well. All the same I mean to have a try at it some day, if I can ever get time. A newspaper man doesn’t have much chance for that sort of thing. I’ve done a good deal of short story writing for the magazines, but I’ve never had the leisure that seems to be necessary for the writing of a book. With three months of liberty I ought to make a start, though—if I could only get the necessary motif for it—the SOUL of the book.  <sub>[v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

> We’ll collaborate,” cried Owen delightedly. “You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.  <sub>[v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

> I’m rather glad the doctor is away,” said Owen slowly. “I wanted to see you alone, Mrs. Blythe. There is something I must tell somebody, or I think it will drive me mad. I’ve been trying for a week to look it in the face—and I can’t. I know I can trust you—and, besides, you will understand. A woman with eyes like yours always understands. You are one of the folks people instinctively tell things to. Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>
